summary: Add happy-path contract coverage and choose response-drift policy
description:
Follow-up from PR #10 review. Runtime OpenAPI response validation is the only coupling between strict response schemas and hand-built handler payloads. Add representative 2xx contract tests for every endpoint and explicitly decide whether production response drift should fail closed with 500 or log and pass through.

Conditions of Success:
- Every documented endpoint has a happy-path test that drives the real handler response through contract middleware
- Tests fail when a handler response drifts from its committed schema
- The production response-drift policy is explicitly chosen and documented
- If the current fail-closed policy remains, operational logging/metrics make contract-generated 500s diagnosable
- make check passes

objective.note: Prevent spec/handler response drift from reaching production unnoticed.

scope.note: Happy-path contract tests for current endpoints plus response-drift runtime policy and observability.

uncertainties.note: Owner decision: retain fail-closed 500 behavior or log and pass through in production.

dependencies.note: Builds on the shared contract middleware introduced by TKT-46.

approach.note: Exercise real handlers through middleware using service fixtures; record the runtime policy in docs/ADR if behavior changes.

first_slice.note: Prove one Commerce 2xx response passes and deliberate drift fails before expanding the table.

success.note: All endpoint happy paths are covered and runtime drift behavior is intentional and observable.

### Readiness — BLOCKED ON POLICY DECISION
Implementation and coverage scope are clear. Before prioritization, the owner must choose whether runtime response-schema drift remains fail-closed with HTTP 500 or becomes log-and-passthrough. The tests are required under either policy.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claim — TKT-47

**Selection reason:** Ticket is in Ready with zero open blockers (only link is `found-in TKT-46`, which is Done). Direct follow-up to TKT-46's contract middleware — the code area is fresh and the COS are concrete.

**⚠️ Gateless run — owner waiver on record.** The repo owner (Mathieu Dupuis) directed this ticket through the full pipeline in fully autonomous mode as a process experiment, explicitly waiving all four human gates for this run only:
- Gate 1 (priority): satisfied by the ticket already being in Ready.
- Gate 2 (plan approval): agent resolves open decisions itself after cross-model critique — prefer the critique's recommendation, else the most reversible option; every self-made decision recorded in plan-final.
- Gate 3 (review + merge): agent squash-merges after the adversarial ai-review converges; review-guide still posted first as the audit record.
- Gate 4 (PO acceptance): agent self-validates each COS against test evidence on merged code.

All other skill rules unchanged: config.models routing, cross-model review for plan and code, TDD red-first, `make check` green before every push, marker comments at each stage, no AI attribution.

**Note on readiness:** `uncertainties` is `open` (owner decision: fail-closed 500 vs log-and-passthrough for production response drift). Under the Gate 2 waiver this decision will be resolved during Planning after the cross-model critique and recorded in plan-final.
